solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Twist perhaps 16 in accommodating answer

parts.note: the answer to 16 down is the Devil, and 'the dickens' is an old name for him, as in 'what the dickens'

indicators.note: accommodating means holding a guest, so the word in takes the letter for answer inside it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a plot twist involving the Devil sits inside the answer to a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' is not a turn of plot but Oliver Twist, the orphan hero of one of Charles Dickens's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is an example of a character typical of the novels of Charles Dickens.

clue.text: Glen is TV presenter's first name

definitions.meaning: a glen is a valley, which in the north of England is also called by this name
the forename of the TV presenter ... Winton, among others

explanation.definitionFit: A valley is both a glen and a dale, and Dale Winton was a well-known British game-show host.

clue.text: Protective clothing from delivery after 22 yards

indicators.note: after puts the delivery word behind the measure

parts.note: a chain is an old measure of length equal to 22 yards, the length of a cricket pitch
mail is what the postman delivers

explanation.surface: Body armour arrives in a parcel after being sent a short distance.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but here it is just a number: 22 yards make one chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Linked metal rings were worn as armour by medieval soldiers to guard against blades.

clue.text: Old legislation is dead

parts.note: ex- means former, as in an ex-wife
an act is a law passed by Parliament

explanation.surface: A law from long ago is no longer in force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead' is used in its sense 'precise', as in 'dead centre' or 'dead right'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead in the sense 'absolutely precise' (dead on time) is a synonym of precise or accurate.

clue.text: Bad-tempered agent guards what's left on ship that's capsized

indicators.note: guards means surrounds protectively, so the agent's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: a capsized ship is upside down, so in a down clue the word port is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A grumpy secret agent watches over the wreck of an overturned vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroppy is British slang for irritable and argumentative, quick to take offence.

clue.text: Broken like what follows

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
in a printed text, what follows comes under what you are reading

explanation.surface: Something is described as shattered in the same way as the next item.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn asunder means split apart into pieces, so the word describes something broken.

clue.text: Composition of soap suds oddly dissolving

indicators.note: the odd letters of the words soap suds melt away, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A bar of soap foams and melts away in the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly dissolving' tells you to lose the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of SOAP SUDS, keeping O, P, U, S.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical work, numbered in a composer's catalogue of compositions.

clue.text: Ruth encompasses Eastern religious behaviour

indicators.note: encompasses means surrounds, so the letter for Eastern goes inside

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity or compassion

explanation.surface: The biblical Ruth takes in Eastern ideas about faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like the woman from the Bible, but it is the old noun meaning compassion, the opposite of ruthlessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoutness, or reverent conduct towards God, is what this word names.

clue.text: Ladies on backs of horses rode round ground — disposed so?

definitions.text: Ladies on backs of horses rode round ground — disposed so?

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so the letters are put in a new order
the backs of these four words are their final letters

explanation.surface: Women once rode horses around the paddock seated in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle LADIES with S, E, D and D, the last letters of horses, rode, round and ground. The whole clue then describes how ladies used to ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Women in long skirts traditionally rode with both legs on one side of the horse on a special saddle.

clue.text: A shopping centre sent back wool

indicators.note: sent back means the words a and mall are read backwards

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Someone returns a woollen item to the shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleece of this South American animal is made into soft wool, so the animal's name stands for the yarn.

clue.text: Parliamentarian with cycle taken in crossing police finally

parts.note: a round is a cycle of events, as in a round of talks

indicators.note: crossing means lying across, so the fooled word straddles the last letter

parts.note: to be had is to be taken in, fooled

indicators.note: finally says to take the last letter of police

explanation.surface: An MP on a bicycle is stopped at a junction by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: A Roundhead was a supporter of Parliament in the English Civil War, named for his cropped hair.
explanation.definitionFit: In the English Civil War the Parliamentarians who fought the Royalists were nicknamed for their short haircuts.

clue.text: Exhausted having ridden wildly round area

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the letter for area
wildly says the letters of ridden are thrown about

explanation.surface: A rider is worn out after galloping around the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' makes DRIEND from RIDDEN, and 'round' puts it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Drained means having all one's energy used up, completely tired out.

clue.text: Teacher keeping a favourite to overturn writer's block

indicators.note: to overturn here means the whole assembly is reversed
keeping means holding, so the teacher's letters go around the other pieces

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A teacher's favourite pupil tries to cure an author's lack of inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's block' is not a creative slump but a block of paper for writing on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of paper sheets is literally a block that a writer uses for jotting.

clue.text: Father avoids a heart operation hell

indicators.note: avoids means stays out of, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: a bypass is an operation to reroute blood around a blocked heart artery
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A father manages to escape having heart surgery, which would have been hell.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottomless pit, or abyss, is a biblical name for the underworld of the damned.

clue.text: Enhanced attraction of chemical 014 apparently

parts.note: James Bond is agent 007, so 014 looks like twice him, and a chemical link of two shared electron pairs is stronger than a single one

explanation.surface: A chemical has an extra-strong pull, as if it were a pair of secret agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 014 is 007 times two: a double James Bond.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry two atoms sharing two pairs of electrons are held together more strongly than by a single link.

clue.text: Gift of the gab is like gold to a politician

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Fluent speech is as precious as gold to anyone in politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in public speaking is what both phrases name: a talent for persuasive talk.

clue.text: Evil one in Newgate for instance

definitions.meaning: Newgate was a notorious London prison long since closed, and nick is British slang for prison

explanation.definitionFit: The Devil has this nickname, and a disused jail like Newgate is a former prison, nick being slang for one.

clue.text: Was a rat left with hereditary element held back?

indicators.note: held means contained, so the left-wing word goes around the other piece

parts.note: red is the colour of the political left

indicators.note: back says the hereditary word is read backwards

parts.note: a gene is a unit of heredity

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether betrayal ran in a left-winger's genes.
explanation.walkthrough: To rat is to go back on a promise or desert a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on a deal means to break one's word, which is to go back on an agreement.

clue.text: Doughboy captures a crude revolutionary

indicators.note: captures means holds inside, so the soldier's letters go around the rest

parts.note: doughboy was slang for an American infantryman, as GI is
ribald means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: An American soldier takes a rough rebel prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: Giuseppe Garibaldi led the fight to unify Italy; a garibaldi is also a currant biscuit, a nod to 'Dough'.
explanation.definitionFit: Garibaldi was the 19th-century Italian rebel leader who fought for unification.

clue.text: Clip lug brawling with bold boxer

indicators.note: brawling means fighting in a disorderly way, so the letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A boxer gives a clumsy oaf a clip round the ear during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' rounds off the picture: a bulldog is a fighting breed, close kin to the boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong spring clip for holding papers is named after the tenacious dog breed.

clue.text: Awkward place to be met urge to change

indicators.note: to change says the letters of met urge are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone feels a sudden impulse to change at an inconvenient moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'up a gum tree' means stuck in a difficult predicament.

clue.text: Wild about education like the USA

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the wild word goes around the education letters

parts.note: feral means wild, as in a feral cat

explanation.surface: Someone is fuming about the state of education in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is a union of self-governing states under a central government.

clue.text: Bridge ploy punishes opponents

parts.note: fines means punishes with a money penalty
in bridge South and East are opponents, as North-South play against East-West

explanation.surface: A bridge player's trick penalises the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four players are named after compass points, N, S, E and W; a pair like S and E sit on opposing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: At bridge this is the play of a lower card hoping a higher opposing card is well placed, a classic tactic.

clue.text: Some misbegotten nuisance having nothing to do

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wretched pest is bored with nothing to keep it busy.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the weariness of idleness, the boredom that comes from lacking occupation.

clue.text: Famous Irish priest missing?

parts.note: no means absent, as in 'no Ted' when he is not there
Father Ted is the Irish priest of the TV sitcom of that name

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a well-known Irish priest has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted was a 1990s sitcom about priests on a remote Irish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known or celebrated, a straightforward synonym for renowned.

clue.text: Taking party from West Indian island, book appropriate transport

indicators.note: taking means removing, so the party letters come out of the island

parts.note: Dominica is an island in the Caribbean
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Leaving a party on a Caribbean island, you should book a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fitting because a minicab is the kind of transport you 'book' by phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A minicab is a private hire car that must be ordered in advance, so it suits a request to book.

clue.text: Explorer gets about on trawler

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
a bot is a program that trawls the internet

explanation.surface: A seafarer goes out on a fishing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trawler' looks like a fishing boat, but it is a web crawler, a bot. John Cabot sailed to North America in 1497.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cabot was an Italian navigator who sailed for England and reached Newfoundland.

clue.text: Make association with success after time

indicators.note: after puts the success word behind the time letter

parts.note: a win is a success

explanation.surface: Someone forms a partnership once they are successful at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Towns are twinned when they form formal links, so the verb means to pair up or associate.

clue.text: Unsuccessful parodies around start of revue — they're on the fringe

parts.note: out means dismissed or failed, as a batsman who is out

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the parodies go around the first letter

parts.note: skits are short comic parodies

indicators.note: start of says to take the first letter of revue

explanation.surface: Failed sketches in a revue end up on the fringe, like a festival sideshow.
explanation.definitionFit: The edges of a town are its suburbs and fringes, the areas furthest from the centre.

clue.text: Half-hearted novelist is inferior

indicators.note: half-hearted says one of the two central letters, the heart of the name, is lost

parts.note: Saul Bellow was an American novelist

explanation.surface: A novelist lacks enthusiasm and so writes second-rate books.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower in rank or quality is what both words mean: one thing ranks under another.

clue.text: Stylish chap expected to possess diamonds

indicators.note: to possess means to hold, so the expected word goes around the diamonds letter

parts.note: due means expected, as in a train due at noon
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A smart man is expected to own diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A dude is a dandy, a man very concerned with his clothes and looks.

clue.text: One walks around in shocking red panties

indicators.note: shocking suggests something jolted out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone strolls about wearing outrageous scarlet underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A person travelling on foot rather than in a vehicle is a walker on the street.
